clue.text: Caper? Museum job ends in prison

indicators.note: in tells us those end letters go inside the word for prison

parts.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail, a prison

indicators.note: ends asks for the closing letter of each of the words Museum and job

explanation.surface: A heist at a museum finishes with the thieves behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes the last letters of Museum and job, M and B, and 'in' puts them inside GAOL. The question mark marks Caper as a noun for a playful leap, not a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a frisky skip or leap, the same playful jump as a frolic.

clue.text: Best outfit naughty gals pull in

indicators.note: in places the word for pull inside the jumbled girls
naughty suggests the letters of gals misbehave and fall out of order

parts.note: taken as written
to drag something is to pull it along

explanation.surface: Badly behaved girls get their best clothes on to attract admirers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' signals the anagram of gals and 'in' the container. 'Pull in' looks like a phrase about attracting people, but 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is an informal idiom for the smart clothes kept for special occasions.

clue.text: Professional filing system?

parts.note: filing here means smoothing fingernails with a file, done professionally in a beauty salon, not keeping papers in order

explanation.surface: An office organisation scheme for documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A beautician shapes and files the nails of the hands in this treatment, which is a sort of filing done for pay.

clue.text: Possesses topless dresses

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its top, its first letter, in this down entry

parts.note: gowns are long dresses

explanation.surface: A risque note about owning some revealing dresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes G, the first letter, from GOWNS.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to have it as your property, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Ace parking by mum, it's clear

parts.note: A is the usual abbreviation for an ace in playing cards
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a mum is a parent

explanation.surface: Someone notices that the best parking space is taken by mother, plain as day.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clear is plain to see, evident, obvious to all.

clue.text: Create a perfect bra with current design

indicators.note: design here means the letters are fashioned into a new pattern

parts.note: taken as written
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: A lingerie maker's slogan about inventing the ideal bra using the latest style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' rearranges A PERFECT BRA together with I to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To prefabricate is to make sections in advance for later assembly, a specialised way of manufacturing.

clue.text: Top primate carrying cross

parts.note: an ape is a primate
X is shaped like a cross

explanation.surface: A leading ape holds up a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: An apex is the highest point or peak of something.

clue.text: Solution for team in rising bother

indicators.note: in places the team inside the upturned word
rising in a down entry means the word for bother reads upwards

parts.note: to rile someone is to bother or annoy them
XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A remedy is sought for a team in growing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns RILE into ELIR, and 'in' sets XI inside it. XI as a team (eleven players) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a medicinal liquid, a potion dissolved in a liquid base.

clue.text: Capital took off after the revolution

indicators.note: after places the word for took off behind the jumbled letters
revolution suggests the three letters of the word the are turned about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
ran means took off, fled

explanation.surface: Someone fled the country following a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' rearranges the letters of 'the', and 'after' places the running-off word behind them. The surface recalls the 1979 Iranian revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Tehran is the capital city of Iran.

clue.text: Blind, headless toadying

indicators.note: headless means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: fawning is toadying, servile flattery

explanation.surface: A flatterer is so servile they seem blind and without a head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' removes F from FAWNING.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind over a shop window is a sheet of canvas giving shade, the same thing as a canopy.

clue.text: Red mullet's always eaten

indicators.note: eaten means the word for always is swallowed inside the word for the mullet

parts.note: a mullet is a kind of fish
ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: Red mullet is a fish that people always eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red mullet' looks like one phrase, the fish, but Red is the definition, meaning flushed; 'eaten' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone running a high temperature is flushed and red in the face.

clue.text: Old man's gone out with raincoat

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly man has gone out wearing his raincoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GONE and RAINCOAT together. The 's of 'Old man's' is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in their eighties is certainly an old person.

clue.text: Fast-moving beam — around the speed of light

indicators.note: around means the beam wraps around the symbol

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
c is the physics symbol for the speed of light

explanation.surface: A light beam travels at nearly light speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts RAY about C.
explanation.definitionFit: Racy can mean lively and spirited, quick in movement, as of a vehicle built for speed.

clue.text: Once a mysterious area

indicators.note: mysterious suggests the letters of once a are puzzlingly mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A place that was once full of mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mysterious' rearranges ONCE A.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean is a vast expanse of sea, a huge area of the globe.

clue.text: Keen backing singer

indicators.note: backing means the word for keen goes backwards

parts.note: avid means keen, eager

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic backing vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen backing singer' reads as one musician, but 'backing' turns AVID round and 'singer' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female singer, especially in opera.

clue.text: Initially it's new gold or tin

definitions.text: Initially it's new gold or tin

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A metallurgist notes that freshly cast gold or tin first takes this shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes the first letters of it's, new, gold, or, tin; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar of cast metal such as gold or tin, newly poured from the mould, is the thing described.

clue.text: Refuse endless grind

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to scrape is to grind or rub harshly

explanation.surface: Refusing to put up with a never-ending daily grind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun, rubbish. 'endless' removes E from SCRAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse is waste matter, bits and pieces thrown away as junk.

clue.text: An antique cabinet?

parts.note: cabinet here means a governing body of ministers, and antique means elderly, so this is rule by old people, not old furniture

explanation.surface: An old piece of furniture for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a system of government by the elderly, so its ministers would be aged.

clue.text: Potential bird sanctuary

parts.note: a protective home for a bird that is not yet hatched, a chick-to-be

explanation.surface: Land that could become a nature reserve for birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin covering of an egg shelters the developing chick, a would-be bird.

clue.text: Coloured Roman Catholic returned one day distracted

indicators.note: returned means those initials go back to front in this down entry
distracted means the letters of one day are thrown into confusion

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Catholic who came back one day was too distracted to do anything but colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns RC into CR; 'distracted' rearranges ONE DAY into AYONED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drawn on in wax pencils has been coloured in.

clue.text: He may offer a real alternative

definitions.text: He may offer a real alternative

parts.words: He may offer a real alternative
parts.note: a real is the currency of Brazil, so this is someone who will give you reals in exchange for your cash, not a man with a genuine option

explanation.surface: A man presents a genuine choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureau de change worker swaps one currency for another, perhaps giving Brazilian reals.

clue.text: Frank carried out after a drink of lager?

indicators.note: after puts the word for carried out behind the can

parts.note: a can is a tin of lager, a drink
did means carried out, performed

explanation.surface: Frank was carried out of the pub after drinking lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name, but it is the adjective, honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Being candid means being open and honest, speaking plainly.

clue.text: He was distressed and disabled

parts.note: read distressed as de-tressed, deprived of his locks: the biblical strongman lost his strength when Delilah had his hair cut

explanation.surface: A man in a sad state, upset and incapacitated.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Judges, the Israelite hero lost his great might once his hair was shorn.

clue.text: Middle class girl's no saint, sadly

indicators.note: middle asks for the central letter of the word class
no means the saint is taken away from the girl

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A middle-class girl, sadly, is no saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle' takes A from cLAss's centre; 'no' removes S from LASS to leave LAS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an interjection voicing sorrow, used like unfortunately.

clue.text: First person detained in big heroin conviction

indicators.note: detained in means the pronoun is held inside the word for big

parts.note: fat means big
I is the first person singular pronoun
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drug dealer is jailed after a big heroin conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detained in' puts I inside FAT, and H follows. 'conviction' means belief, not a guilty verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: Faith is firm belief, a deeply held conviction.

clue.text: Glimpse end of century by telepathy

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, covers telepathy

indicators.note: end of asks for the final letter of century

explanation.surface: Seeing the end of the century through mind reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes Y from century.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of something, a brief look.

clue.text: Riddle surrounding female's pose

indicators.note: surrounding means the word for pose goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a woman's posture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle but is the verb meaning to sieve. 'surrounding' puts SIT round F.
explanation.definitionFit: To riddle soil is to pass it through a coarse sieve, sifting it.

clue.text: A revolutionary figure is a pain

parts.note: Che Guevara is the famous Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: A revolutionary is a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull, persistent pain.

clue.text: Depress girl with gin, for example

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
gin is an example of a spirit

explanation.surface: A woman drinking gin feels low.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispirit someone is to dishearten them, lowering their mood.

clue.text: Vet show on TV

definitions.meaning: to vet is to check or examine candidates
to broadcast a programme is to put it on air

explanation.surface: An animal doctor presents a television programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet is to check people for suitability; to broadcast a film or programme is to put it out on the box.

clue.text: Meaning concealed within code? Not in general

indicators.note: concealed within says the letters lie inside the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A message with its meaning buried in a code, though not in general use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed within' points to the letters running through coDE NOT IN General.
explanation.definitionFit: Denoting means signifying, standing for or indicating.

clue.text: Elvis opening with version of 'devil in disguise'

indicators.note: version of means the letters are given in a different form
opening asks for the first letter of the name Elvis

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Elvis opens his concert with a cover of the song Devil in Disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' takes E from Elvis; 'version of' rearranges E with DEVIL. (You're the) Devil in Disguise was a 1963 Elvis Presley hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in disguise is masked or hidden behind a covering.
